target_customer: Online furniture shoppers, with retailers as the implied channel since the pipeline built AR models from any retailer's product pages
problem: Shoppers cannot tell how a piece of furniture will look or fit in their home before buying it online.
business_model: Consumer AR app; monetization not stated in any source found (retailer referral or licensing implied)

founders.name: Rohan Relan
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the only founder and gives no background; no other source about his background was found.

exit.reason: No public statement found; the YC directory only marks the company Inactive.

competitors.name: IKEA Place
competitors.what: IKEA's ARKit app for placing virtual furniture in a room, released with iOS 11

competitors.name: Wayfair View in Room 3D
competitors.what: AR furniture preview in the Wayfair app, on iOS first via ARKit and on Android in March 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Turning arbitrary retailer product pages into AR-ready 3D models needs a computer vision pipeline, which was hard for a one-person team, although ARKit launched in 2017 and handled tracking.

defensibility.rationale: The platform layer (ARKit, ARCore) was free to everyone and big retailers shipped their own AR viewers within months, so there was no data or network moat; the any-retailer model pipeline was the only differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: IKEA launched IKEA Place in September 2017 and Wayfair extended its AR view to Android in March 2018, so large retailers built the same wedge in-house.

market_need_then: Furniture is a high-return, high-uncertainty category online, and Apple's ARKit (iOS 11, 2017) had just made consumer AR practical; the YC listing shows the pitch but no usage numbers were found.

branding.domain_note: miruhome.com now redirects to a domain broker listing (HugeDomains), so the domain lapsed and is for sale; no purchase history found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand was found; searches returned only directory listings, and the name is shared with an unrelated window company and a later YC robotics startup.

outcome_analysis: The cause of the shutdown is not public. The YC directory marks the company Inactive and the website domain is now parked for sale. The company was a one-person team building an AR furniture previewer just as IKEA Place and Wayfair shipped AR viewers on the same Apple and Google AR platforms, so the wedge was being taken by well-resourced retailers. No funding, traction or post-mortem was found, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Searches for a shutdown, funding, press and brand story found only directory listings (YC, Altss). A CB Insights page showing a $20M Series A in 2024 belongs to a different company called Miru (formerly Click Materials) and was excluded. A YC Summer 2024 robotics startup also uses the name Miru. The miruhome.com fetch redirected to a domain broker, so the site is treated as dead. The YC page lists only one founder.
